_comment: Canonical per-node PipeWire sink volumes for the yard show. Keyed by NODE id
from config/animatronics.json (NOT characterId) so the values feed straight into
node scripts/yard-theater/verify-moment.mjs <moment.json> --volume-map 2=1.50,3=1.30,4=0.55
READ THIS BEFORE TRUSTING THE NUMBERS:
1. wpctl sink volume is NODE-LOCAL RUNTIME STATE. It is not in git, it is not
deployed by npm run deploy:all, and it does NOT survive a reboot or a
redeploy. This file is a RECORD, not a mechanism -- something has to apply it.
Re-apply per node and re-check with scripts/fleet-audio/earcheck.mjs.
2. Values above 1.00 are software gain above unity. They CANNOT be set through
PUT /api/system/volume or PUT /api/orchestration/volume -- both take an integer
percent 0-100 and clamp there. Above 1.00 is wpctl-only. The apiSettable field
below is the best each node can do inside that 0-100 clamp.
3. The wpctl volume curve is approximately CUBIC, measured on these rigs:
gain_dB ~= 60 * log10(v2/v1). Orlok 0.65->1.00 predicted +5.6 dB, measured
+5.4 dB. Small changes move a lot -- 0.55 vs 0.40 on node 4 is 10.4 dB.
4. Absolute dBFS is NOT comparable ACROSS nodes: each figure is that node's own
microphone, and mic-to-speaker distance differs per rig. Treat the dB as a
per-node instrument. The cross-node anchor is the operator's ear.
5. Run-to-run repeatability is about +/-2 dB. Do not read a 1 dB difference as real.
6. TUNED ON SPEECH ONLY. Every measurement here is a single TTS line, which peaks
around -7.5 dBFS. The audio-library files peak at 0.0 dBFS (median mean -14.3),
so on the nodes above unity -- 3 at 1.30 and especially 2 at 1.50 -- a loud
music/SFX cue will HARD-CLIP where the spoken line did not. Not measured: no
library cue was played at 1.30/1.50. Check that before the show if loud cues
run through those two nodes.
method: Each node speaks its own in-character cast phrase in its own voice while that
node's own microphones are already open. castDb is the p90 frame envelope of the
capture in dBFS; riseDb is castDb minus that same mic's median noise floor;
recall is the fraction of the cast phrase's words ElevenLabs Scribe read back.
The 18s window (default is 13s) is deliberate: a window that clips the tail of a
slow line scores as GARBLED on a node whose audio is perfect.

nodes.name: Orlok
note: 1.50 measured no louder than 1.30 (-21.5 vs -19.2/-21.2), but that gap is
inside the +/-2 dB run-to-run spread, so this is NOT proof of clipping --
it is only evidence that 1.50 buys nothing measurable. 1.30 is chosen as
the lower setting that already reaches the plateau. Recall stayed 100% at
every level, so nothing here is distortion-limited.

nodes.name: Mina
nodes.note: RE-MEASURE. The 1.50 figure was tuned on the C-Media Unitek Y-247A, which was removed 2026-08-20 along with the USB hub. This node now outputs through a reSpeaker XVF3800 (same model as Orlok, whose measured figure is 1.30). Unity is a safe placeholder, not a measurement - re-run earcheck and record.

nodes.name: Sir Dragomir
note: He is the outlier rig, and it is NOT the USB adapter -- all three nodes run the
same Unitek Y-247A, and his ALSA hardware Speaker control is actually 2 dB LOWER
than the other two (33/37 vs 35/37). The extra loudness is downstream of the Pi.
0.85 -> 1.00 gained only +0.4 dB against a cubic-predicted +2.1, and recall fell
94% -> 69%: his amp is compressing/limiting near the top. Do not run him above
~0.85, and there is no reason to -- 0.55 already matches the fleet.
0.40 drops him to riseDb 9.1, which is thin for a yard. 0.55 is the floor.
